cultural.vision_reason: This is a European engraving illustrating Chinese figures from Nieuhof's 17th-century travel account of an embassy to China; "Cham" in the title refers to the "Grand Tartar Cham" (Khan) emperor, not the Cham ethnic group of Vietnam, and the image depicts Chinese, not Cham, dress.

physical.title: print; costume print; book-illustration
physical.summary:
Two Chinese women and a child conversing in foreground, more figures seen behind in a square; illustration to Johannes Nieuhof's 'An Embassy from the East-India Company of the United Provinces, to the Grand Tartar Cham Emperor of China' (London: 1669, Figures XV and XVI); letterpress on verso.

cultural.vision_reason: This is a 17th-century European travel engraving from Nieuhof's account, depicting Chinese women (not Cham) in a European illustrator's imagined style, from a book about an embassy to China's "Grand Tartar Cham Emperor" — the "Cham" here refers to the Qing emperor's title, unrelated to the Cham people of Vietnam.

physical.title: print; costume print; book-illustration
physical.summary:
Two Chinese women standing with a little girl at left in foreground, more figures seen behind outside huts among palm trees; illustration to Johannes Nieuhof's 'An Embassy from the East-India Company of the United Provinces, to the Grand Tartar Cham Emperor of China' (London: 1669, Figures VII and VIII); letterpress on verso.
